memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Roast it and eat it at the place the Lord your God will choose. Then in the morning return to your tents. For six days eat unleavened bread and on the seventh day hold an assembly to the Lord your God and do no work. - Deut 16:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the sacred meal, the people were told to go back to their tents in the morning and continue the week of unleavened bread, ending with a solemn assembly and rest. Worship did not stay locked inside one holy evening. It flowed out into ordinary days and finally gathered the people back together again to rest before God.

This is a beautiful pattern, remembering, returning to daily life, and then resting in worship. The encounter with God was meant to shape the whole week, not just one night. God cares about both our gathered worship and our scattered, everyday living.

We can fall into thinking that worship is only what happens in a service, and then live the rest of the week as though God were far away. But the God who met Israel at the Passover walked with them back to their tents. In Christ, our worship and our daily life belong together. We gather to remember His finished work, and then we carry that remembrance into our homes, our work, and our rest. The command to cease from work on the seventh day pointed ahead to the deeper rest we find in Jesus, who invites the weary to come to Him (Matt 11:28). Let your worship reach every corner of your ordinary week.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does your worship shape your ordinary days, or stay separate?
2. How can you carry Sunday's truth into Monday's routine?
3. Where do you most need Christ's rest right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, let my worship flow into every part of my week. Draw me into the rest I find only in Jesus. Amen.
